subject: Hosted API: elevated p95 latency — status advisory & mitigation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Skyline Analytics <ops@skyline.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API: elevated p95 latency — status advisory & mitigation

Hi Nadia / Skyline team,

Quick note to let you know we’re seeing an elevated p95 on generation/initiation for your account in US-WEST since ~08:50 UTC. Impact: increased tail latency for synchronous generation endpoints (p95 up from ~420ms to ~1.8s). We’ve posted an incident on our status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incident/2026-08-21-p95-drift

What we know so far:
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: rwinf/gpt-large-2026-quant)
- Scope: a subset of tokens/requests showing longer initiation times; not all requests are affected
- Window: began ~08:50 UTC, continuing at time of this note

Immediate actions we’re taking:
- Routing a portion of Skyline traffic to a lower-latency pool to reduce p95 (non-disruptive fallback)
- Enabling additional prefix/KV prefetching for your account to reduce cold-path penalties
- Turning on a temporary 1.5s client-side retry recommendation (we will provide guidance)

We’re attaching a snapshot of the p95 chart for your team (p95-dash-20260821.png). I’ll follow up with a short postmortem and remediation plan once the triage completes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects critical flows.

Next steps for you:
- We recommend deferring non-critical bulk scoring jobs for the next 2–3 hours while we stabilize routing
- If you prefer, we can escalate to burst dedicated capacity for a short window (requires approval)

I’ll be on standby on this thread and in case we need to set up a quick bridge.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: [Internal] Triage update — p95 drift (Skyline)

Folks — quick internal update and recommended mitigation steps (summarized for the customer in a follow-up message).

Root-cause hypothesis so far (runtime telemetry + traces):
- We observed a surge of requests with atypical short-lived sessions that exhaust the KV prefix cache eviction budget for the serving pool handling Skyline traffic. That caused a higher-than-normal fraction of requests to take the cold execution path during initiation (KV lookups + kernel fallback), which pushes p95 up.

Actions taken (implemented 12:10–12:30 UTC):
- Route 30% of Skyline traffic to a warmed dedicated pool to reduce cold-path exposure (non-disruptive failover).
- Temporarily increased KV cache allocation for the affected pool (runtime config change).
- Deployed a targeted request-shaping rule at the edge to smooth short bursts (burst window: 30s).
- Rolled out a prefix prefetcher tweak for Skyline’s model profile (should reduce initiation by ~300–600ms on affected requests).

Customer-facing checklist to send now:
- Confirmed routing change is live; ask Skyline to run a quick smoke test hitting /v1/generate and report p95
- Offer to enable a 1-hour dedicated burst if they want immediate headroom (I’ll coordinate pricing/approval)

Attaching the mitigation playbook for CS/SEs: mitigation-playbook-v1.pdf

I’ll draft a concise postmortem and recommended long-term fixes (model-aware cache sizing + improved detection of cache exhaustion patterns).

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Hosted API: incident summary & next steps (post-incident)

Hi Nadia / Skyline team,

Thanks for your patience today. This is a short post-incident summary and action items.

Timeline (UTC):
- 08:50 — first p95 elevation detected for Skyline (alerting triggered)
- 09:12 — customer advisory issued (status page up)
- 12:10 — routing + KV allocation changes applied; targeted edge shaping rule rolled out
- 12:30 — observed p95 return close to baseline for majority of traffic
- 13:05 — monitoring confirms sustained stabilization; we reverted temporary routing by 16:30 after validating behavior

Root cause (summary):
- A concentrated pattern of short-lived sessions from a subset of Skyline workloads caused repeated prefix cache evictions in the serving pool that handled your traffic. This increased the fraction of requests hitting the cold KV path during initiation, which manifested as an elevated p95.

Immediate remediation (already applied):
- Temporary reroute to warmed pool and increased KV allocation for affected pool
- Edge request-shaping to smooth bursty patterns
- Prefix prefetch adjustments for Skyline’s model profile

Planned follow-ups (next 2 weeks):
- Implement model-aware cache sizing for your account to prevent future eviction storms
- Add a customer-specific detection rule to alert on sudden cache eviction rate increases
- Review traffic pattern recommendations and provide a short checklist for your release teams to avoid short-lived session bursts during peak deploys

Compensation: We’ll apply a 10% service credit for the affected billing window. I’ve opened a billing ticket and included the HubSpot ID: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/67890.

If you’d like a quick 20-minute bridge to walk through the technical details with Dylan and our runtime team, we’re available tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks again and apologies for the impact — please reply here if anything reappears.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
